acceptanceCriteria: A recorded decision chooses the remedy (per-spec sharding, uncommitted derived index with CI check, or another) with its effect on spec-requirements-check, specindex tests and agent read routes.
A reproduction with two branches that each add a requirement to a different spec merges in both orders without textual conflicts in generated files.
Existing doc gates and agent routes that read REQUIREMENTS.tsv / INDEX.json keep working or are migrated in the same change.
body: Observed 2026-10-16 on beamfall/corvint#961 (V1-1449 et al.): added to the merge queue five times (13:12, 14:41, 18:03, 19:55 UTC) and removed each time without a single merge_group CI run (13:12:02 -> 13:12:17; 19:55 -> 20:13:27 when main moved). git merge-tree against origin/main shows the textual conflict in docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv every time another PR adding requirements lands first; on the same afternoon #985, #991 and #993 went DIRTY the same way (INDEX.json, README.md, REQUIREMENTS.tsv, plus delivery-status lines in docs/specs/corvint-tasks-agent-leases-v0.md), and GitHub disarmed their auto-merge. Each repair costs a merge commit, a regeneration, a push and a full CI run while Actions runs ~2 concurrent runs. Expected: two PRs that add requirements to different specs (or different sections) merge in either order without a textual conflict in generated files. Actual: any two spec-touching PRs conflict on the generated files. Options to evaluate: shard the generated index per spec (one generated file per spec), stop committing derived files and check them in CI only, or make rows order/line-stable so appends from different specs land on different lines. Spec delivery-status lines that every lane appends to are a second, smaller hotspot.
title: Generated spec index files (REQUIREMENTS.tsv, INDEX.json, specs README.md) conflict between every pair of concurrent spec PRs, so the merge queue ejects PRs before CI runs
